candidate.derivedAnswer: B, the radius of the smaller circle
candidate.answerReason: The tangent-radius right triangles are similar, giving center distances from D in the ratio 3:1. Their difference is the center separation 4r, so D is 2r from the smaller center and r from B.

methods.label: Compare the tangent right triangles
methods.explanation:
Let \(r>0\) be the smaller radius. Let \(O\) and \(P\) be the centers of the circles with diameters \(AC\) and \(CB\), respectively. Since \(AC=3CB\), their radii are \(3r\) and \(r\). The centers are the diameter midpoints, so the points occur in the order \(A,O,C,P,B\), and
\[
OP=OC+CP=3r+r=4r.
\]
Let \(T\) and \(U\) be the respective contact points of the common tangent. The radii \(OT\) and \(PU\) are perpendicular to that tangent. Thus the right triangles \(DOT\) and \(DPU\) are similar: each has a right angle and the same acute angle between \(AB\) and the tangent. Consequently,
\[
\frac{DO}{DP}=\frac{OT}{PU}=3.
\]
The point \(D\) cannot lie beyond \(A\), because then \(DO<DP\). Therefore it lies beyond \(B\), where \(DO=DP+OP=DP+4r\). Hence
\[
3DP=DP+4r,
\qquad DP=2r.
\]
Since \(PB=r\), we obtain \(BD=DP-PB=r\). Thus \(\boxed{BD\text{ is the smaller radius}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
